name: vehicle-purchase-visual
description: Visual check: purchase vehicle deducts cost from cash, mesh appears in scene, fleet shows idle state. Vehicle purchases are made by clicking the dealership rows in the Fleet panel (issue #479), not by typing `vehicle buy`; the list/scores steps stay observation commands.

steps.description: cash:100000 is set here, on `campaign start`, because this is the step that decides the level's cash: createGameForLevel builds a fresh GameState from dusty_hollow's own $50,000, so a bump on a `new_game` before it would be discarded. $100,000 covers both purchases below (debris_hauler $25,000 + drill_rig $35,000) with headroom, so the Fleet panel's dealership buttons for both are enabled and a real player click lands.

expect.note: the cash: override replaces dusty_hollow's $50,000 default outright

real click on the Fleet panel's debris_hauler tier-1 row -- vehicle buy debris_hauler with no tier: arg defaults to tier 1 too (parseVehicleTierArg, vehicle.ts), so command mode and this click target the same purchase

steps.description: A second real purchase from the same open panel: $75,000 in hand against a $35,000 drill rig, so the dealership row is enabled and clicking it buys the rig. The awaitUsable ahead of the click is the affordability assertion -- the Fleet panel disables a tier row whenever cash < purchaseCost (setTierButtonAffordable, FleetPanel.ts), so a run that had underfunded this step would fail here rather than quietly buying anyway. No toolbar click: the Vehicles panel is already open from the hauler purchase, and re-clicking the toolbar entry would close it.

expect.note: $75,000 - $35,000; both purchases stay in the black, which is the whole point of funding the level properly instead of overdrawing
